name: VA-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +18 partisan lean
Walkinshaw's massive financial advantage ($2.8M raised vs ~$11K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
Incumbent running in a seat the party already holds
model.rationale: The district's +18 Democratic lean, Walkinshaw's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 97% all point to a safe Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings contradict that picture.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending against Walkinshaw would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 11th District leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent James Walkinshaw is seeking a full term after winning the seat. He has raised about $2.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, with substantial outside support, while Republican Arthur Purves has raised only about $11,000 with almost no cash remaining. A Green candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 97%. The combination of a strong partisan lean, incumbency, and a lopsided resource advantage makes an upset unlikely.
